comments.author: @Katiramro
comments.text:
Where Did the Rasuwa  Flood Really Come From?
Having crossed the Rasuwa–Gyirong border at Rasuwa Gadhi both on my way to and returning from Kailash, I have seen the geography of the area firsthand. After watching the footage showing the massive Immigration Building being swept away, I was struck by an important observation: Lende Khola generally flows from east to west, yet the Border Immigration Building appears to have been forcefully pushed from north to south. This raises a serious question about the actual direction and source of the flood.
If the flood had originated primarily from Lende Khola, the direction of destruction would generally be expected to correspond with its east–west flow. However, the available visual evidence does not appear to show Lende Khola initially overtopping its banks or spreading significantly beyond its channel. In fact, people can be seen crossing the Lende Khola bridge from the Immigration Building. This raises the possibility that the main destructive surge may have come from the Trishuli River, potentially carrying a massive volume of water and debris from the upstream watershed in China/Tibet. In other words, the primary source of the disaster may not have been Lende Khola.
This hypothesis must be independently and scientifically verified through rigorous hydrological and forensic analysis—including satellite imagery, flood-flow modelling, terrain and river-channel analysis, debris-deposition patterns, and the direction of displacement of buildings, vehicles, trees, and other structures. Determining the actual source and flow path of the flood is critical not only to establishing what happened, but also to preventing similar disasters in the future.
